title: Protocol for UVC Uridine Actinometry
author: Pousty, Mamane, et al.
materials: •Laboratory absorbance scan apparatus with reference sensor according, e.g., spectroradiometer (using an Ocean Optics USB4000 spectroradiometer equipped with a cosine corrector, OCF- 104447, EOS-A1241604), or radiometer.•Petri dishes, e.g., Disposable Petri dishes polystyrene, diameter 87 mm, Pyrex®, diameter 30 mm. Note that the Petri dishes do not have to be disposable, and the diameter may vary, this factor is considered in Eqs. (3) and (4).•100 mL volumetric flask.•Micropipettes with disposable tips, e.g., 50, 100, 200, 10,000 µL.•Spectrophotometer for measurements in the spectral range 200–400 nm, with a spectral resolution Δλ = 2 nm and a sensitivity of 0.1 mAU (Thermo Scientific Evolution 220 double beam UV-Vis spectrophotometer, THS840-210600S).•5 cm quartz cuvette.
All reagents must be analytical grade.

steps.title: Prepare Solution A (UV-free water)
steps.instruction: Prepare double-distilled water free of UV absorbing substances.

substeps.instruction: Record the spectrum from 200 to 400 nm using a 5 cm cuvette.
Verify that absorbance A is less than 0.002 at 254 and 262 nm.

steps.title: Prepare Solution B (1 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.0)
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 mM phosphate buffer solution.

substeps.instruction: Add (2.5 ± 0.05) mL of a colorless standard buffer solution (phosphate buffer solution pH 6.88, approx 0.04 M) to a 100 mL volumetric flask.
Fill to the mark with Solution A.
Test for sufficiently low absorbance as described for Solution A.

steps.title: Prepare Solution C (Uridine stock solution)
steps.instruction: Prepare a 7.4 ± 0.2 mM uridine stock solution in water.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 180 ± 5 mg of uridine (≥99%, MW 244.2 g mol-1) in 100 mL of Solution A.
Store the stock solution in a dark refrigerator at 4°C with an aluminum foil cover for up to one week.

steps.title: Prepare Uridine calibration test solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a fresh test solution in buffer with an absorbance ≤ 0.1 at 262 nm based on the irradiation path length (d).

substeps.instruction: Select the volume of stock solution for a 100 mL volumetric flask based on path length: for d=0.5 cm (e.g., 30 mL in 87 mm Petri dish), use 200 µL; for d=1.0 cm, use 100 µL; for d=1.5 cm, use 65 µL; for d=2.0 cm, use 50 µL.
Add the stock solution to the flask using a micropipette.
Fill to the mark with 1 mM buffer (Solution B) and mix thoroughly.
Control quality by recording the spectrum from 200 to 400 nm in a 5 cm cuvette to determine the initial absorbance Ao at 262 nm.

steps.title: Set up UV exposure apparatus
steps.instruction: Prepare the collimated beam apparatus using a low-pressure UV lamp or UV-LED lamp, maintaining a solution temperature between 20 and 25 °C.

substeps.instruction: Switch on the UV lamp for approximately 30 min for thermal stabilization.
Adjust the distance between the lamp and the Petri dish so the irradiance is approximately 1.5 W/m2 (0.15 mW/cm2).
Verify homogeneity across the Petri dish (less than ± 2% deviation) by scanning with a UV sensor every 5 mm in x and y directions.

steps.title: Measure incident photon flux
steps.instruction: Determine the irradiance and calculate the incident photon flux q0(253.7).

substeps.instruction: Position the radiometer/spectroradiometer detector head so the 'calibration plane' is level with the top of the washer/ring mask or cardboard plate.
Record the irradiance value E(253.7) at the center of the hole in the ring mask.
Calculate q(253.7) using the formula: q(253.7) = E(253.7) × PF / (0.1196266 / (253.7 × 10-9)), where PF is the Petri Factor.

steps.title: Perform Uridine actinometry irradiation
steps.instruction: Irradiate the sample at equal time intervals to achieve a >50% drop in uridine concentration.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the maximum irradiation time tmax = 6.97 × 10 / Estim (sec), where Estim is the estimated irradiance in W/m².
Divide the irradiation period into four equal intervals (e.g., 30 min intervals).
Stop irradiation at each interval by closing the shutter.
Transfer a portion of the solution into a dry 5 cm quartz cuvette and measure absorbance at 262 nm.
Transfer the solution back to the Petri dish (ensure remnants in cuvette are < 250 µL, verified by weighing).
Repeat for all intervals to obtain absorbance values Ao, A1, A2, and A3.

steps.title: Calculate results
steps.instruction: Determine uridine concentrations and decomposition rates.

substeps.instruction: Calculate uridine concentrations (M) using the molar absorption coefficient εU(262) = 10,185 M–1 cm–1.
Plot the concentrations against exposure time in seconds to determine the slope.
Determine the irradiation time t50 for 50% decomposition by plotting log(At/Ao) versus irradiation time; the intercept at log(At/Ao) = –0.3 is t50.
